name: The Ahwar of Southern Iraq: Refuge of Biodiversity and the Relict Landscape of the Mesopotamian Cities
description: In southern Iraq, where the Tigris and Euphrates fan out toward the Gulf, this site combines four vast wetland marshes with the ruins of three Sumerian cities: Uruk, Ur and Eridu. The marshes form one of the world's largest inland deltas, a green maze of reeds and water amid scorching desert. Beside them stand settlements dating back some 5,000 to 6,000 years, and some scholars have called the region the "Garden of Eden.
